entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adalgott (died 1165) was Bishop of Chur in the Rhaetian Alps from 1150 to 1165, one of the most strategically positioned sees in medieval Europe. Chur controlled the Alpine passes — particularly the routes through the Splügen and Maloja passes — that connected Germany and the Low Countries with Italy, making its bishop a figure of considerable importance in the geography of medieval trade, pilgrimage, and imperial politics.

Bishop of Chur during the tumultuous reign of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, Adalgott navigated the period of Barbarossa's Italian campaigns and the competing pressures of imperial and ecclesiastical politics in the Alpine corridor. Chur was both an ancient Roman city (Curia Raetorum) and a medieval Alpine crossroads, and its bishop held rights over key mountain passes that gave him economic and strategic leverage.

Adalgott's episcopate contributed to the continuing development of Chur as a centre of Alpine ecclesiastical culture. The Diocese of Chur had been one of the most important in the Carolingian ecclesiastical system, and it retained strategic significance in the Hohenstaufen period. His tenure maintained the see's institutional dignity during a period of considerable Alpine political complexity.
